Born in South Dakota in 1968, he graduated from the University of Colorado at Boulder in 1992. He has worked for [[Wizards of the Coast]] since 1997, before that he worked at [[TSR, Inc.]] starting in 1995. He currently lives in the greater Seattle area. In 1998 he won the Origins Award for Best Adventure for ''Return to the Tomb of Horrors''.<ref name="CordellBlog">[http://web.archive.org/20080512133523/brucecordell.blogspot.com/2003/05/about-bruce.html http://brucecordell.blogspot.com]</ref>
Bruce is [[List of Planescape quotes|referenced a number of times]] in Planescape material as "[[Ucec Ordell]]."

{{Plane | image = | caption = | name = Brux | othernames = | symbol = Beastlands.png | demonym = | natives = [[Mortai]] | languages = | fork-material = [[Gold]] | fork-note = F | fork-chord = major | fork-audio = F major.ogg | basicrefs = <ref name="MotP3e-pp141-144">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|141-144}}</ref><ref name="Dr120-p42-43">{{Cite dragon/120/Plane Speaking|42-43}}</ref><ref name="MCII2e-p66-67">{{Cite book/Monstrous Compendium Planescape Appendix II|66-67}}</ref> | type-GW = Layer | shape-size-GW = Infinite | gravity-GW = Normal | time-GW = Normal | morphic-GW = Divinely | element-energy-GW = None | alignment-GW = {{Alignment grid|off|on|on|off|off|off|off|off|off}} | magical-GW = Normal | layers-GW = | layer-number-GW = 2 | location-GW = the [[Beastlands (plane)|Beastlands]] | refs-GW = <ref name="MotP3e-pp141-144" /> | type-WA = | shape-size-WA = | gravity-WA = | mutability-WA = | element-energy-WA = | alignment-WA = | magical-WA = | layers-WA = | layer-number-WA = | location-WA = | refs-WA = | type-WT = | shape-size-WT = | gravity-WT = | time-WT = | morphic-WT = | element-energy-WT = | alignment-WT = | magical-WT = | faith-WT = | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = | inhabitants = yes | deities = yes | locations = yes | organizations = yes | settlements = yes | usethe = | useon = }} '''Brux''' was the second layer of the [[Beastlands (plane)|Beastlands]]. A realm locked in perpetual twilight, it contained the [[divine realm]]s of [[Deneir]], [[Milil]], [[Haela Brightaxe]], and the [[cat lord]].<ref name="PoC2e-p22-25">{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Benevolentiae|22-25}}</ref><ref name="OHG2e-p181">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|181}}</ref><ref name="DD2e-p67-71">{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|67-71}}</ref>
==Geography== The sun appeared as a red orb always touching the horizon of Brux, while a half moon could be seen hanging low on the opposite side of the sky. It was considerably cooler than [[Krigala]], so fog and mist commonly rose from the ground and obscured the trees. All trees grew slanted on the layer, pointing toward the dim source of light of the perpetually setting sun, and created long shadows. This seemingly frozen state could be disconcerting to visitors, but it did not disturb the activity cycle of the animals that lived there.<ref name="MotP3e-pp141-144" /><ref name="PoC2e-p22-25" />
The layer had an abundance of creeks and streams that led to Krigala and eventually flowed into the [[Oceanus]].<ref name="MotP3e-pp141-144" />
==Notable Locations== * The [[Cat Lord's Prowl]], realm of the [[cat lord]].<ref name="PoC2e-p22-25" /> * [[Findar Endar]], realm of [[Haela Brightaxe]].<ref name="DD2e-p67-71" /> * The [[Library of All Knowledge]], shared realm of [[Deneir]] and [[Milil]].<ref name="OHG2e-p181" /><ref name="FA2e-p54">{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|54,116}}</ref> * [[Ursis]], realm of [[Balador]].<ref name="PoC.LB-p25">{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Benevolentiae|25}}</ref>
==Inhabitants== The layer's main inhabitants were animals whose activity cycles peaked around dawn and dusk, such as [[tiger]]s, [[bat]]s, and [[fox]]es.<ref name="PC-LB2e-p16">{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Benevolentiae|16}}</ref>
[[Ferrix]], the playful goddess of [[Weretiger|weretigresses]], had no permanent realm but roamed twilight Brux freely.<ref>{{Cite book/Monster Mythology|114}}</ref><ref name="OHG-176">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|176}}</ref>

It contained the [[divine realm]]s of [[Azuth]] and [[Savras]], as well as [[Heliopolis]], the shared [[divine realm]] of [[Ra]], [[Isis]], [[Osiris]] and [[Horus]] of the [[Pharaonic pantheon]].<ref name="PL2e-p18-24" /><ref name="OHG2e-p173,181">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|173,181}}</ref><ref name="PP2e-p47">{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|47}}</ref>
==Geography== Although similar to the first layer [[Abellio]], with its orderly plains dotted with mountains, hills, forests, lakes and streams, Buxenus was also a highly organized war camp, training site, and mustering ground for armies bent on reconquering [[Nemausus]]. Outside of divine realms, the whole layer was controlled by the [[Harmonium]], who guarded entrances and exits, and whose scattered camps housed soldiers and prisoners.<ref name="PL2e-p18-24" />
==Notable Locations== * [[Azuth (realm)|Azuth]], realm of [[Azuth]]. It was a cavern whose entrance was hidden in the side of a hill, opening into a descending stairway that led down to a series of chambers filled with marvels.<ref name="PL2e-p18-24" /> * [[The Eye]], realm of [[Savras]].<ref name="PP2e-p47" /> * [[Heliopolis]], shared realm of [[Ra]], [[Isis]], [[Osiris]] and [[Horus]]. It was a triangle-shaped realm divided in thirds, each controlled by Isis, Osiris, and Ra. Horus wandered between the realms and did not hold a territory of his own.<ref name="PL2e-p18-24" /> * [[Melodia]], the home town of the [[Harmonium]].<ref>{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Arcadia|19-21}}</ref>
==Inhabitants== Outside of the few divine realms, the entire layer was run by the Harmonium, who used it as a mustering ground to send forces into Nemausus. They also ran prison camps for chaotic creatures, hoping to condition them into a lawful worldview, often resorting to violent means. Unwittingly, the evil of these camps done in the name of "greater good" was causing the layer to gradually shift towards neutrality and into [[Mechanus]], as had already happened in Nemausus.<ref>{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Arcadia|23}}</ref> The faction heavily patrolled the entire layer, guarding all entrances and exits known to them, and turning back all travelers.<ref name="PL2e-p18-24" />

[[Shurrock]] | layer-number-GW = | location-GW = | refs-GW = {{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|73}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|75}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|78-82}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|136-138}} | type-WA = | shape-size-WA = | gravity-WA = | mutability-WA = | element-energy-WA = | alignment-WA = | magical-WA = | layers-WA = | layer-number-WA = | location-WA = | refs-WA = | type-WT = | shape-size-WT = | gravity-WT = | time-WT = | morphic-WT = | element-energy-WT = | alignment-WT = | magical-WT = | faith-WT = | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = | inhabitants = yes | deities = yes | locations = yes | organizations = | settlements = yes | usethe = | useon = }} The '''Twin Paradises of Bytopia''' were two layers that formed one of the [[Outer Planes]] in the [[Great Wheel cosmology]] model representing alignments between [[lawful good]] and [[neutral good]].{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|58}} Some characteristics of this plane were ascribed to the [[World Tree cosmology]] planes of [[Golden Hills]]{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|155}} and the [[House of the Triad]]{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|159}} when that cosmology became popular. The Golden Hills became part of [[Arvandor]] after the [[Spellplague]] and the House of the Triad became known as [[Celestia]]{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|62}} as described by the [[World Axis cosmology]]. {{Quote |No jink for your dinner? No problem. There's a roof that needs fixing — hop to it, lads! |Kendia, Bytopian innkeeper.{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/A Player's Guide to Conflict|12}} }} ==Description== The two layers of this plane were joined at one barrier which happened to span the entire sky at about 10 miles (16km) above sea level. Gravity for each layer was normal for that layer but switched direction as soon as one crossed the barrier. The inhabitants of one layer could look up and see the other layer hanging upside down high overhead. Several mountains reached the crossover point and a few met mountains rising up from the other side, allowing careful climbers a way to reach the other layer. Also the space between layers was filled with air, allowing flight from one side to the other. Each layer glowed with a golden-white light. ===Dothion=== {{Main|Dothion}} Dothion was a bucolic land of old forests and huge meadows subject to mild seasonal changes and gentle weather. Portals to [[Seven Heavens]], [[Elysium]], and [[Concordant Opposition]] were found in caverns as brightly glowing patterns: concentric circles for the Seven Heavens, radiating lines for Elysium, and both patterns superimposed, which resembled a spider web, for Concordant Opposition. Travelers from the [[Astral Plane]] would emerge from the ''color pools'' on this layer. ===Shurrock=== {{Main|Shurrock}} Across the barrier, Shurrock had much the same landscape features but much harsher weather: summers were hot and winters were long and cold. Storms were more common here, with booming thunder and heavy rains. Life on the Shurrock side was more challenging and kept the inhabitants busy, but both sides were virtuously industrious. ==Inhabitants== The animals in the Twin Paradises were sentient with average intelligence or above, but did not have the ability to speak. Some trees were also intelligent, similar to [[treant]]s from the [[Prime Material Plane]]. The usual menagerie of [[upper planes|upper plane]] creatures were found here, including [[solar]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|111}} [[planetar]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|101}} [[hollyphant]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|75}} [[deva]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|42}} [[foo creature]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|65}} [[baku]],{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|12}} and [[agathia]].{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|9}} Inhabitants of the plane created a type of [[Bytopian Stout!|stout]]{{Cite book/For Duty & Deity|9}} and a type of aromatic [[spice]]d [[nutbread]] with [[carrot]]s and [[almond]]s. It was served in thick slices and tasted mildly sweet. These products could be found sold in the planar city of [[Sigil]].{{Cite game/Planescape: Torment}} ==Realms== {{/Imagemap}} * [[Baervan Wildwanderer]] the Forest Gnome, once had a realm in Dothion, among [[Golden Hills|those]] of the rest of his [[Lords of the Golden Hills|pantheon]]. Baervan's tree, an ancient oak called [[Whisperleaf]], grew on the side of a mountain that connected to a similar mountain on the Shurrock side.{{Cite book/Unearthed Arcana 1st edition|117}} * [[Baravar Cloakshadow]] the Sly One, [[Gnome|gnomish]] god of deception, had his realm named the [[Hidden Knoll]] in Dothion protected with many traps.{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|141}}{{Cite book/On The '''cant''' is the particular form of slang popular in [[Sigil]] in particular, but it's spread through much of the [[Outlands]] and other [[Outer Planes]].
== A == * '''addle-cove''': An idiot.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref><ref name="dvd124">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=124}}</ref> * '''Anarchist''': A nickname for a member of the [[Revolutionary League]].<ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''anthill''': A city or town.<ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref>
== B == * '''bang around''': To spend idle time in.<ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''bar that''': A nearly-polite way of telling someone to shut up, or not to talk about a subject.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''barmy''': Insane. Barmies are typically those who have been "touched" by the impossible infinities of the planes.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref><ref name="dvd124">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=124}}</ref> * '''basher''': Neutral reference to a person, although often a thug or fighter.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref><ref name="dvd124">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=124}}</ref> * '''berk''': A fool, especially one who should know better.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref><ref name="dvd124">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=124}}</ref> * '''birdcage''': A cell or prison.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''Bleaker''': A member of the [[Bleak Cabal]].<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref> * '''blinds''': Anything impossible or hopeless, referring to the dead ends of the [[Mazes]].<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''blood''': An expert or professional. A mark of high respect.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref><ref name="dvd124">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=124}}</ref> * '''bob''': The business of cheating someone out of something.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''bone-box''': The mouth, named because of the teeth inside it. "Stop rattling your bone-box."<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''box''': A [[rogue modron]] who has taken up residence in [[Sigil]].<ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''brain-box''': Someone's head, usually not in a complimentary way. "Go soak your brain-box" is a common idiom.<ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''bub''': Booze, usually the cheap sort.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref><ref name="dvd124">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=124}}</ref> * '''bubber''': One who imbibes ''bub'': a drunk, especially one who has fallen on hard times.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''burg''': Any town smaller than Sigil, either in size or in spirit. (The towns in question may disagree with Cagers' assessment.)<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref>
== C == * The '''Cage''': A nickname for Sigil (q.v. ''birdcage''), since there's no way in or out except through one of the Lady's portals.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref><ref name="dvd124">{{b|D&D|Die Vecna Die!|pdf=17483|nip=1|page=124}}</ref> * '''Cager''': A native or resident of Sigil.<ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''canny''': Smart or talented.<ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * '''case''': The house where other location where someone lives. Has a positive connotation.<ref name="pscssato95">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=95}}</ref><ref name="pwhb150">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=150}}</ref> * the '''chant''': The news, facts, local gossip. [[Agathys]] | layer-number-GW = | location-GW = | refs-GW = {{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|73}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|75}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|78-82}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|103}}{{Cite book/The Halfling's Gem|273,278,279}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|104-108}} | type-WA = [[Astral dominion]] | shape-size-WA = Six archipelagos under starless sky | gravity-WA = | mutability-WA = | element-energy-WA = | alignment-WA = | magical-WA = | layers-WA = | layer-number-WA = | location-WA = | refs-WA = {{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition}} | type-WT = | shape-size-WT = | gravity-WT = | time-WT = | morphic-WT = | element-energy-WT = | alignment-WT = | magical-WT = | faith-WT = | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = | inhabitants = yes | deities = yes | locations = yes | organizations = yes | settlements = yes | based = [[wikipedia:en:Tartarus|Tartarus]] (Greek) | usethe = | useon = }}The '''Tarterian Depths of Carceri''' ({{Pronounce|car|SEHR|ee|refs={{Cite book/Hellbound: The Blood War/The Chant of the War|7}}}}) , also known as '''Tarterus''',{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|56}} was an [[Outer Plane]] in the [[Great Wheel cosmology]] model representing alignments between [[chaotic evil]] and [[neutral evil]].{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|58}} Situated between [[Hades]] and the [[Abyss]], Tarterus was a plane of contention between the warring [[demon]]s and devils but few of those interlopers would challenge the native [[demodand]]s. {{Quote |This ain't a prison my friend, it's ''the'' prison. |Planewalker [[Alanna Haladrin]].{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Malevolentiae|6}} }} ==Description== The six layers of Tarterus had a seemingly infinite number of worlds arranged like a string of pearls stretching into the air-filled void. In the top layer, Othrys, each orb was about the size of a [[Prime Material Plane|Prime Material]] world and averaged about {{SI|100|mi|k|long=yes}} from the nearest orb. In each successive lower layer the planetoids grew smaller and farther apart. There was no sun but the soil of each orb gave off heat and a dull reddish glow, similar to the phosphorescence of fire [[beetle]]s. The planets did not rotate and there was no day or night unless a [[greater deity]] wished it so in their realm. Seasons and weather occurred randomly and what little plant life there was would rapidly mature after rainfall and then wither hours later. Each orb was connected to one specific Prime Material world.{{Cite book/Song of the Saurials|300|20}} The barriers between layers were always located at the deepest points on each planetoid and always lead to the same sphere in the next layer, so the worlds of Tarterus can be imagined as spheres nested like [[Wikipedia:Matryoshka doll|Matryoshka dolls]] and each layer contained a string of orbs of a particular size. ===Othrys=== {{/Imagemap}} {{Main|Othrys}} The first layer of Tarterus was named for Mount Othrys which was really two mountains on two adjacent orbs (both also called Othrys) each about {{SI|50|mi|k|long=yes}} high joined together at the peaks in a massive citadel. The worlds of Othrys were so close together that a traveler could easily fly from one to the next. For those who did not wish to fly, the river [[Styx]] flowed through all the worlds of this level in the usual mystical fashion. Many other rivers fed the Styx, and the surfaces of this layer were mostly marsh, bogs, and [[quicksand]]. Othrys was the brightest (due to the proximity of equal-sized worlds on either side) and warmest layer; no worse than a hot summer day on the [[Prime Material Plane]]. Other than the mountains, the ground was soft, like peat, and cut by deep chasms. Othrys could be reached via the [[Astral Plane]] and had portals to the [[Abyss]], [[Hades]], and [[Concordant Opposition]].{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|74}} Long ago it could be reached via [[Mount Olympus]], but when the Olympian gods overthrew the Titans they used their combined might to shatter the part of the mountain that connected to Tarterus, thus trapping the Titans on this plane.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|105}} ===Cathrys=== {{Main|Cathrys}} The planets of the second layer were smaller than those of Othrys and about {{SI|500|mi|k|long=yes}} apart. Plant life in this layer was both abundant and deadly. The flora in the overgrown jungles and grasslands secreted acid that could eat through metal in a minute or less. ===Minethys=== {{Main|Minethys}} The third layer of Tarterus had planetoids smaller than those of Cathrys which hovered about {{SI|5000|mi|k|long=yes}} apart. The air between orbs was torn by harsh winds which carried poisonous dust storms from world to world, making most surfaces a barren desert. Huge tornadoes periodically swept through, carrying anything in its path to distant locations or even an adjacent orb. ===Colothys=== {{Main|Colothys}} The worlds of the fourth layer were spiked with colossal mountains rising above deep chasms. Hundreds of miles/kilometers from base to peak, the terrain of this layer made the orbs more asymmetrical than in other layers. Adjacent orbs were {{SI|500000|mi|k|long=yes}} apart so they appeared to be small spiky red moons in the utterly black sky. Legions of [[demon]]s and [[daemon]]s made lairs in the canyon walls. ===Porphatys=== {{Main|Porphatys}} Black, acidic rain and snow assailed the many worldlets of the fifth layer from giant black clouds that moved between them. On individual worlds, islands barely higher than sandbars came up over the waves of shallow, cold oceans.{{Cite book/Stormwrack|9}} The snow only stuck to the peaks of any mountains, melting to cover the rest of the surfaces with {{SIrange|1|6|ft|c}} of a weak acid that did not affect metal or stone but could eat away cloth in a minute or less. All barriers between this layer and the next were under water. The orbs of Porphatys were millions of miles/kilometers apart and barely discernible even when not blocked by demonic clouds. A pilotless vessel called the [[Ship of One Hundred]] endlessly sails the seas of Porphatys. ===Agathys=== {{Main|Agathys}} The smallest, coldest planetoids occupied the sixth layer and were so far apart that neighboring orbs could not be seen at all. Every surface was covered in dark ice that showed streaks of red and the air was so cold it made breathing difficult. If any layer existed beyond Agathys, the barriers would have been buried under miles/kilometers of ice. ==Inhabitants== The dominant race that inhabited Tarterus were the winged [[demodand]]s. Shators were the ruling nobility,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|34}} typically controlling major portions of an orb. All but the most powerful [[daemon]]s and [[demon]]s would avoid them. Also found on this plane were [[nightmare]]s, [[achaierai]], and [[shadow demon]]s, with reports of [[mephit]]s,{{Cite book/Fiend Folio 1st edition|64}} [[hordling]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|75}} and [[vargouille]].{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|123}} The [[Companions of the Hall]] entered Tarterus by means of the [[Taros Hoop]].{{Cite book/The Halfling's Gem|271}} ==Realms== ==Geography== According to the [[Great Wheel cosmology]], the Caverns of Thought were located deep underground beneath the [[Outlands]] and were connected to the [[Gzemnid's Realm|realm]] of the [[beholder]] deity [[Gzemnid]].<ref name="OHG2e-p136,176" /><ref name="PPO2e-p29" /> The [[World Tree cosmology]] established the realm as part of the [[Fiendish planes|fiendish plane]] of the [[Deep Caverns]].<ref name="PGF3e-p148-149" />
In both cosmologies, however, the Caverns of Thought were described as a hostile place wrought with inaudible yet clear and powerful thoughts that slowly drove its visitors mad until they were reduced to thoughtless zombies.<ref name="OHG2e-p136,176" /><ref name="PGF3e-p148-149" /> This effect was a consequence of Ilsensine's power prying into the minds of the realm's visitors in search of their secrets.<ref name="PCS-SB2e-p32-33">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/Sigil and Beyond|32-33}}</ref>
The realm was a labyrinth of tunnels that were lit by the faint glow of fungus. It was avoided even by [[fiends]].<ref name="PPO2e-p29" /> The [[dwarf]] inhabitants of the nearby realm of the [[Dwarven Mountain]] also avoided digging their tunnels too close to the Caverns.<ref name="OHG2e-p136,176" />
The only creatures that dared visit the realm were motivated by the search for knowledge that Ilsensine possessed. However, the price he demanded was high, often leading to the visitors' losing part of their own minds.<ref name="PPO2e-p29" />

{{Plane | image = | caption = | name = Celestial Nadir | othernames = | demonym = | natives = | languages = | basicrefs = <ref name="FRCG"/> | type-GW = | shape-size-GW = | gravity-GW = | time-GW = | morphic-GW = | element-energy-GW = | alignment-GW = | magical-GW = | layers-GW = | layer-number-GW = | location-GW = | refs-GW = | type-WA = [[Astral dominion]] | shape-size-WA = | gravity-WA = | mutability-WA = | element-energy-WA = | alignment-WA = | magical-WA = | layers-WA = | layer-number-WA = | location-WA = | refs-WA = <ref name="FRCG">{{cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|140}}</ref> | type-WT = [[Demiplane]] | shape-size-WT = | gravity-WT = | time-WT = | morphic-WT = | element-energy-WT = | alignment-WT = | magical-WT = | faith-WT = | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = <ref name="DV" /> | inhabitants = | deities = | locations = | organizations = | settlements = | usethe = | useon = }} The '''Celestial Nadir''' was an artificial [[demiplane]] created by the original [[Imaskari Empire]]. It was used as a safe place for magical experimentation should unforeseen consequences arise.<ref name="DV">{{Cite book/Darkvision|215–217, 253, 279–280, 284–285}}</ref> It also served as a magical bridge for the [[Imaskari]], since many portals were situated in the demiplane that led to various locations on the [[Prime Material Plane]].<ref name="LoP-11">{{cite book/Lady of Poison||11}}</ref>
==Access== It could only be accessed from certain locations possessing standing-stone rings, and only by using a Celestial Nadir keystone. All the keystones were lost by the 14{{th}} century [[DR]], save for one possessed by [[Ususi Manaallin|Empress Ususi]]. There were said to be twenty standing-stone rings that led to the Celestial Nadir. However, the only known standing-stone ring locations, as discovered by Empress Ususi, were the [[menhir]] ring at [[Adama's Tooth]], the [[Mucklestones]] ring in the [[Forest of Lethyr|Lethyr Forest]], and an unnamed ring in [[Skyclave]] city (formerly the [[Palace of the Purple Emperor]]).<ref name="DV" />
==Features== The plane was an apparently endless void, with roads of unsupported stone. It had free-floating lakes and islands of stone, which held a number of crumbled ruins. Some of those ruins had illumination, which may have accounted for the stars.<ref name="DV-C2">{{cite book/Darkvision||2}}</ref> The tombs of many powerful emperors drifted within some of the ruins.<ref name="DV-C26">{{cite book/Darkvision||26}}</ref> Some other objects floating through the void included cubes made of perfect mirrors, and slabs of transparent glass with the remains of monsters embedded in them.<ref name="DV-C25">{{cite book/Darkvision||25}}</ref> Both were prisons holding monsters in stasis.<ref name="LoP-11"/> The air inside the demiplane was sharp and cold, but not damp, with a faint hint of the smell after a thunderstorm<ref name="DV-C25">{{cite book/Darkvision||25}}</ref><ref name="LoP-11"/> and occassional sharp breezes.<ref name="LoP-11"/>
The stones at Adamas' Ring led to a three-way split. One of the roads continued for a few hundred paces to a geode where Pandorym's body was held; the path around the geode was overgrown with celestial nadir crystal. Another road led to an aurora-like curtain after a few miles, behind which the Palace of the Purple Emperor was faintly visible. It served as a portal to the same. The third path seemed to lead off into the distance beyond what was visible. There were dot-like stars both above and below.<ref name="DV-C25">{{cite book/Darkvision||25}}</ref> The path from the Mucklestones was straight for as far as the eye could see; Ususi employed it to reach Yeshelmaar sooner.<ref name="LoP-11"/> A different path opened into the [[Arches of Xenosi]] in the [[Rawlinswood]], close to [[Dun-Tharos]].<ref name="LoP-14"/>
The Celestial Nadir was home to a naturally occurring sediment called [[Plangent|celestial nadir crystals]], which were amethyst in color.<ref name="DV" /> It could be found in geode-like hollows, even inside of statues, strangely.<ref name="LoP-11"/> There were as well creatures formed of astral ectoplasm, naturally occurring [[astral construct]]s, and large spheres of accumulated moisture, which held fishes inside.<ref name="LoP-11"/> Time passed differently in the center of the demiplane relative to the edges, according to Ususi.<ref name="LoP-14">{{cite book/Lady of Poison||14}}</ref>
==History== Originally devised by the Imaskari to serve as a buffer between [[portal]]s, and then extended to serve as a dumping ground for unwanted experiments, refuse, creatures drawn from other planes, hazardous extraplanar material and a safehouse for valuables, the Nadir continued to grow after the destruction of the Imaskari, perhaps even absorbing other demiplanes.<ref name="LoP-11"/>
In {{yearlink|-2488}}, the [[Elder evil]] [[Pandorym]] was summoned by the Imaskari, and its body was separated from its mind, leaving it inside the Celestial Nadir.<ref name="DV-219-223">{{cite book/Darkvision|219-223}}</ref> The elder evil remained imprisoned until [[Vaelan]] miners working for the [[Datharathi]] accidentally stumbled upon the Nadir in {{yearlink|1370}}.<ref name="TGHotR-150">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|150}}</ref> It was resealed after Ususi Manaallin and others entered the Celestial Nadir in {{yearlink|1374}}.<ref name="TGHotR-155">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|155}}</ref>

{{main|World_Tree_cosmology#Celestial_Planes}} '''Celestial planes''' is a collective term used to describe a subset of the [[Outer Planes]] in the [[World Tree cosmology]] model. The celestial planes were generally associated with the [[good]] deities whereas the [[fiendish planes]] were generally associated with the [[evil]] ones.<ref name="PGtF-140">{{Cite book/Player’s Guide to Faerûn|140}}</ref> The celestial planes were: # [[Arvandor]] # [[Brightwater]] # [[Dwarfhome]] # [[Dweomerheart]] # The [[Gates of the Moon]] # [[Golden Hills]] # [[Green Fields]] # The [[House of Knowledge (plane)|House of Knowledge]] # The [[House of the Triad]] All of these planes were connected to the [[World Tree]] which could be used to travel directly between planes without having to pass through the [[Prime Material Plane]], but this mode of travel was often dangerous.<ref name="PGtF-140" />

The '''Cerilian [[power]]s''' represent the primary powers of the continent of ''Cerilia'', on the world of [[Aebrynis]].
Around [[Prehistory|1398 BFHR]], the gods of the people of ''Cerilia'' fought the dark power Azrai in the War of Shadow. The War culminated in the Battle of Mount Deismaar, in which they sacrificed themselves in order to defeat Azrai for good.
Although they all perished, their closest mortal servants absorbed much of their power, and themselves ascended to godhood. All of Cerilia's current pantheon of gods can trace themselves to this event.

The '''City Provisioner's''' was once [[Sigil]]'s only storehouse for food and grains, although there are more now. It was operated by the [[Tribe of One]] faction prior to their destruction at the [[Lady of Pain]]'s hands.

[[Kurtulmak]] lived in another warren of caves, [[Draukari]]. The caves were narrow, short, muddy, and so twisted that it was very easy to get lost and get ambushed by an angry tribe of kobolds.<ref name="PGtF-pp147-148" />
[[Maglubiyet]] resided in a fort called [[Grashmog]], the Hearth of Battle. Grashmog served as a temple and training camp for [[clerics]] and [[warriors]]. The most feared ones were the [[Steelbiters]], respected for their bond with the fiendish [[winter wolf]] mounts.<ref name="PGtF-pp147-148" />

[[File:Clerks Ward map.jpg|thumb|right|400px|A map of the Ward]] The '''Clerk's Ward''' is one of the six wards of [[Sigil]]. It's home to the upper middle classes, and is the city's administrative hub and center of its bureaucracy. It was also home to the headquarters of the [[Fated]], [[Sign of One]] and [[Society of Sensation]] factions.
Long ago in Sigil's history, more than 10,000 years ago, the Clerk's Ward was known as the '''Ward of Masks'''.

The '''Clueless Rebellion''' was an event in [[Sigil]]'s history sparked by an explosion of tensions in the [[Prime Ward]], which led to it becoming the [[Lower Ward]].
== History ==
Long ago, [[prime]] newcomers to Sigil were herded into the Prime Ward by the [[Incanterium]] and [[Sodkillers]], who didn't want the Clueless to get in the way of their business. The primes would figure out the lay of the land and how to survive in the city, at which point they were no longer Clueless, and presumably would be allowed greater access to the rest of the city.
Primes did not take well to their effective incarceration, a cage within the Cage, and tensions mounted. They noticed that their section of the city had portals which tended to lead to the [[Lower Planes]]. In protest, the Clueless started opening these portals as often as possible, letting through whatever they could. Rumor has it that a particular item called the [[Shadow-Sorcelled Key]] was used by [[Nameless One|the rebellion's leader]] to open every lower-planar portal at once.
While the smarter fiends knew not to cause trouble in Sigil, most of the creatures who came through were the mindless hordes of lower-ranking fiends. They ravaged the Prime Ward and its surroundings until the Lady herself took action. Everyone who participated was killed. The fiends and the rebellion's leader vanished. The [[dabus]] did their best to repair the mess, but much of the gloom and noxious fumes from the Lower Planes continue today. The Shadow-Sorcelled Key was thought by many to have been taken by the Lady, to prevent a re-occurrence. Some, however, suspect it may have been lost, and waiting to be rediscovered somewhere in the Ward.
Due to the Rebellion and its devastation, the boundaries of the Ward expanded, and rather than risk a repeat of the events, the Ward was renamed the [[Lower Ward]]. It took a long time for the area to recover, remaining almost abandoned for some time, but the construction of the Great Foundry re-invigorated the area, although it contributed to the continued poor air quality.

[[File:Color pool.png|thumb|right|280px|''A pair of travelers in the [[Astral Plane]], one of whom is about to step into a color pool.'']] '''Color pools''' were gateways that led from the [[Astral Plane]] to other [[planes of existence]].{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|62-63}}{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|25}}{{Cite book/The Planewalker's Handbook|31}}{{Cite book/A Guide to the Astral Plane|30-33}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|48}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|16}}{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|47}} Sometimes also called '''color veils''', these "pools" were scattered about the Astral Plane and unique to it, and they were the most common feature of that endless expanse. The plane to which a pool led could sometimes be determined by the pool's color. Most scholars believed that there were an infinite number of color pools to any given plane adjacent to the Astral, yet at the same time, some planes seemed easier to reach by color pools than others. ==Locations== [[File:Githyanki pirates.jpg|thumb|right|250px|''Githyanki pirates traveled from color pool to color pool looking for victims.'']] While color pools were plentiful and likely the most common feature to be seen by a visitor to the astral, this was relative to the vast size of the Astral Plane. It would usually take a visitor to the Astral anywhere from 6 to 24 hours of astral travel to reach the nearest color pool from any given point.{{Cite book/A Guide to the Astral Plane|13}} Even so, one didn't have to know the precise location of any color pool; if you were to visit the Astral Plane, you only had to think about going to a pool leading to your desired destination and you would eventually find such a pool. If you had been to that planar destination before, you would find an appropriate pool even more quickly, though not a particular pool to a particular place on that plane. One strange matter reported by astral travels from [[Faerûn]] was that once a visitor to the Astral focused on a pool of a certain color, it was impossible to observe a pool of any other color during that entire visit to the Astral Plane.{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|139}} [[Githyanki]] pirates often cruised from color pool to color pool in their [[astral skiff]]s, searching for victims.{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide v.3.5|155}} ==Description== Color pools seemed to viewers like irregularly shaped, shimmering disks of opaque color in the otherwise monochrome space of the Astral Plane. Sometimes, they appeared more like wisps or other shapes than like circular pools. They were two-dimensional, being infinitely thin on the edge and about 10 to 60 feet (3 to 18 meters) in diameter. Some sages supposed them to be composed of a mixture of "liquid reality" mixed with "astral energies". {{fq | float = right | width = | text = …coalescing basins of spacetime around pinprick holes in reality that allow a tiny bit of the true world into the Silver Void. | source = One planewalker's description of a color pool. }} Color pools were only visible from one side, which could be problematic, as they were functional from any direction; one could easily pass through the invisible side, without even being aware of doing so, and appear instantly in another plane of existence.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|66}} ===Pool Colors=== A strange feature of the magic of color pools was that the pool through which one entered into the Astral always appeared silvery in color to the traveler. Such silver pools seems very much like rippling [[mercury|liquid mercury]]. If travelers had entered by means of an ''[[astral projection]]'', their [[silver cord]]s led back into this silver pool. It was said that all other pools had a color that indicated their destination, but some scholars of the planes warned that this idea of a "color code" for the pools was dangerous nonsense. Even if not nonsense, the assumption was still a dangerous one, as it was possible to change the hues of the pools using magic. {{fq | float = right | width = | text = Whoops. | source = A fool thinking that he'd figured out the "color code" for color pools. }} Those planar scholars who believed in the existence of alternate [[Material Plane]]s said that the pools to such planes were always of metallic colors other than silver, such as bronze or brass. All other planes supposedly had non-metallic colors for their pools. For example, a color pool leading to the [[Ethereal plane]] was like a whirlpool of watery milk. For the pools leading to any other plane, the colors described by the sages were remarkably consistent, and are provided in the table shown here.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|49}} {{Planar navigation}} ==Travel== Every [[Outer Plane]] could be reached from the Astral through a color pool, and the pool led most often to the first layer of any plane. The two exceptions to this were [[Cynosure]] and the [[Fugue Plane]], which could never be reached through a color pool.{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|148,153}} When a traveler entered through a color pool in an astral form, the silver cord extended into the new plane, and a physical form was instantly created for the traveler appropriate to the new plane. The silver cord remained connected, all the way back through the color pool, through the Astral, and through the silver-colored pool back to the traveler's original body, which remained in stasis. It was impossible to enter the Astral with ''astral projection'' and return to the original plane through any other color pool except the one through which the Astral had been entered. Other color pools back to the original plane would simply cease to function. If a spellcaster using ''astral projection'' took a group along, everyone else in the group was instantly pulled through the color pool once the spellcaster had passed through; they had no choice in the matter, and the magic of the spell forced them along. A traveler who had managed to enter the Astral plane in physical form had no such limitation. For her or him, passing through any color pool physically and instantly transported both body and mind to the new plane, even if it was another location on the plane of origin. In any case, to an observer on the destination plane, a traveler would simply appear out of nowhere. {{fq | float = right | width = | text = Take a walk,
Take a swim,
But stay thee from a color pool.
Watch me run,
Watch me fly,
But stay thee from a color pool. | source = An ancient children's rhyme heard in [[Sigil]]. }} Where exactly a color pool led on the destination plane varied greatly; it could be in the sky, underwater, underground, or on the surface. Unlike ''[[portal]]s'', the destinations of color pools were not intelligently planned; they were random. Moving through a color pool felt like forcing oneself through a thin, soft membrane, or through warm molasses, which resisted and surrounded the traveler until giving way, at which point, the traveler burst through to the other plane. It was not possible to insert only a portion of one's body through a pool; the entire body had to pass through at once, as soon as enough force was applied to break through the "membrane". Only about fifteen to thirty{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide v.3.5|154}} percent of color pools allowed returning from the destination plane; the rest were essentially a means of "one-way" travel. A "two-way" pool was not invisible at the other end but appeared as a gaping hole in reality into the Astral Plane. Most such two-way pools were guarded closely by the inhabitants of the destination plane. These portals could even be moved to other locations. Many were used for interplanar trade, and a few trading towns had been founded around them. Two-way color pools were one cause for the presence of non-astral creatures found in the Astral Plane on occasion and for many other large astral objects.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|51}} An even smaller number of color pools were both two-way and immovable. Such cases were called "fixed portals". ==Scrying== It was possible to see through a color pool like a window to its destination if the viewer concentrated intently on the pool from within a close range of about 10 yards (9 meters). If the viewers were using an ''astral projection'', only the caster of that spell could see through the pool to the other side. If a group of planar travelers had entered the Astral Plane physically by other means, then the most intelligent individual could control the result of the viewing. When observed with such mental concentration, the pool ceased being opaque and became fully transparent, providing a view from between 100 and 400 yards (90 and 370 meters) above the surface of the target plane. If the viewer were mentally capable enough, he or she could attempt to focus the image toward a particular place on that plane, but the location viewed might still be anywhere on that plane despite this. Using a color pool like a [[scrying]] pool in this way was termed "using an astral window". Viewing the destination plane in this way in no way changed the actual location one might arrive at if the color pool were entered. Once a location had become visible, the scrier on the Astral plan could actually move the image around at a rate dependent on her or his intelligence, at a maximum rate of about 6 miles (9 kilometers) per hour. Strangely, moving the image around was much slower in areas with high magical activity, such as cities with a large population of wizards. Moving one's vantage point in such a way did not permit passing through solid objects or through any space smaller than the diameter of the color pool itself. It was possible to use this technique to scry into large buildings, if their ceilings were high enough. Placing a thin strip of lead within the structure of a ceiling could defend against such unwanted observation from the Astral Plane. It was not possible to cast a spell through an "astral window" from the Astral side. Some creatures or powerful spellcasters could sense when they were being scried on in this way and fog up or seal off the color pool or even attack the scrier on the other end. Color pools could only be sealed off slowly, however, shrinking in size until vanishing, and it was usually possible for the scrier and any companions to pass through the pool to the destination, if they desired to do so before it fully closed. To detect such a scrying attempt through a color pool usually required a spell or magic item such as ''[[see invisibility]]'' or ''[[true seeing]]''. Creatures that could harm a scrier by attacking back through the color pool when viewed included monsters with gaze attacks, such as [[basilisk]]s, [[cockatrice]]s, or [[medusa]]s. Once someone had used a pool to scry on its specific destination, the destination would not change for a length of time equal to a day on the Material Plane. Using a pool as an astral window wore out the viewer, and the average [[human]] could only carry out such observation for under two hours. The window would remain focused where the viewer left it for up to ten hours before reverting, and it could not be used to scry again for at least 20 hours after that. Observing through a color pool to the Ethereal came with an additional risk of being accidentally sucked into the [[ether cyclone]] on the other side. All color pools from the Astral to the Ethereal led into the heart of an ether cyclone; it was impossible to scry anywhere else on the Ethereal plane. ==History== Some planar scholars postulated that color pools were the result of damage caused to the fabric of existence of the Astral Plane caused by all of the magical travel through it. Unlike [[planar conduit]]s, which seemed to age and may have been created by some higher powers for a purpose, color pools seemed ageless and random in their placement. More pessimistic folk suggested that the increasing interplanar travel was leading to more frequent psychic storms as a result of the weakening caused by the pools. ==Notable Color Pools== One of the manifold color pools to the Material Plane had its terminus in the [[Thrall Caverns]] in [[Oryndoll]], at a place known as the [[Void Pool]]. This was, naturally, a matter of concern to the [[mind flayer]]s of Oryndoll, since it would have allowed the hated githyanki entrance into their city. The illithids failed at every attempt to destroy or move the terminus of the one-way color pool. They maintained observation of the Void Pool at all times because of this.{{Cite book/Drizzt Do'Urden's Guide to the Underdark|84-85}} ==Appendix== ===See Also=== * [[Yggdrasil]], the branches or roots of which passed through portals similar to color pools.{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|45}} * [[Mount Olympus]], from which caverns led through similar portals to other planes. ===Appearances=== * ''[[City of Gold]]'' ===References=== {{Refs}} [[Category:Planar pathways]]

'''Common''' is, as the name suggests, the most common language used by humanoids on the [[Prime Material plane]] in order to communicate with each other.
While many species have their own racial language, and learn Common as a secondary language, humans tend to learn Common as their primary language. As such, it's a language sometimes associated with humans rather than as a language for mutual trade and communication.
Common is said to have originated in [[Sigil]], which may conflict with the claim that [[Planar Common]] developed from the Common spoken by visitors to Sigil from the Prime.<ref name="dnd5e37">{{b|D&D|Player's Handbook 5.5|page=37}}</ref> Common and Planar Common are similar enough that speakers can mostly understand each other.
Common also has an associated sign language for those who cannot hear, or those who wish to otherwise communicate non-verbally.
== Usage ==
In [[125 YFHR]], a [[Riddling Skeleton]] in the [[Dead Nations]] posed a riddle to [[Puzzled Skeleton|another skeleton]]: "''Think of words which end in '-GRY.' Angry and hungry are two of them. There are but three words in the Common Tongue... what is the third word? The word is something that one uses every day. If thou hast listened carefully, I have already told thee what it is.''"
The riddle's answer was "tongue" as there are three words in "The Common Tongue."
== Background Information == * "Common" is meant to be the fantasy equivalent of whatever language the players speak: e.g. for English-speaking players, Common would be English.

The '''Concordant Express''' is a clockwork locomotive created by [[modron]]s, which travels throughout the planes. Tickets are presented as paper-thin sheets of brass.
The sapient Engine Car is the train's conductor, featuring a face much like a [[monodrone]]. The wheels are a delicate network of interlacing cogs. A series of mechanical arms from the front of the train rapidly places new sections of track which levitate above the ground, so terrain poses no problems. A similar series of arms behind the Caboose collects the track segments as the train passes them, and then delivers them back up to the Engine Car.
The Express is powered by treasure; with two monodrones shoveling coins and gems into a massive furnace in the Engine Car. The furnace consumes a minimum of 100GP per hour.
The train has access to seemingly invisible portals that only the Engine Car can find, allowing it to pass through multiple different planes on its journey. Its "home station" is on [[Regulus]] in [[Mechanus]], accessed via the misnamed [[Concord Terminus]] station in [[Automata]].
A [[quadrone]] used to oversee hospitality on the Express, but after receiving conflicting orders from two [[pentadrone]] superiors, it went rogue, calling itself [[Glitch]].
== Layout == The train reconfigures as needed for each voyage, which may or may not include one or more of the following:
* '''Abacus Car''': A car with ten monodrones and a [[duodrone]] calling itself the "Math Wizard." When asked a mathematical question, the monodrones hold up numbered placards and arrange themselves to display the resulting number. A chalkboard details the reason why the [[Great Modron March]] occurs every 289 years. * '''Aquarium Car''': A car flooded with water, although magic keeps the water from escaping through open doors (including drying any passengers who leave). The car contains coral, algae-covered statues, and tiny fish. * '''Cargo Car''': A car containing goods for transport and trade. * '''Jail Car''': A soundproof car twice the height of other cars, encased in thick iron. Each floor has four cells, allowing for the transport of up to eight prisoners per car. Spiral staircases connect the two floors, and a balcony serves as panopticon. * '''Planartarium Car''': A hologram of a quadrone calling itself "Cosmo" stands before a brass model of the Outlands, with symbols indicating other Outer and Inner Planes. For a donation worth at least 10gp, Cosmo will tell travelers about any of the planes. * '''Passenger Car''': A car with three passenger compartments and two privies for passengers traveling to another destination. Monodrone valets Higglesworth, Bot, and Orb are available for passengers. * '''Temple Car''': A car for worship. The outer walls are stained glass, the floor has patterned rugs, and decorative columns support a vaulted mosaic ceiling.
== Destinations == According to the Planartarium, the Express travels through the [[Inner Planes]], the [[Outlands]], and the 16 [[Outer Planes]] of the [[Great Ring]]. It's unknown if it also travels to the [[Prime Material plane]], to its co-existent [[Shadowfell]] and [[Feywild]], or to the transitory [[Ethereal plane]] and [[Astral Plane]].

'''Cosmic realignment''' is a process by which, if a location on the [[Outer Planes]] begins to embody the nature of a different plane too closely, the location, and its inhabitants, will shift to the target plane. For some inhabitants, this is desirable; other elements try to prevent it from occurring.<ref name="paitmsato61">{{b|Planescape|Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse|page=61, Sigil and the Outlands}}</ref>
This phenomenon is most often witnessed with the [[Gate-town]]s, 16 locations around the [[Outlands]] built around a permanent portal to one of the other Outer Planes on the [[Great Road]].
== Known Instances ==
In [[Ribcage]], the [[gate-town]] to [[Baator]], if one travels through the gate, they'll find themselves in the ruins of [[Darkspine]] on [[Avernus]], the first layer. Darkspine was the previous gate-town to Baator; once it arrived, it was attacked by fiends and blasted by fireballs common to Avernus. A few survivors eke out a living, but it's largely abandoned.<ref name="fod25">{{b|Planescape|Fires of Dis|pdf=17273|page=25}}</ref>
Even though each plane is infinite in scope, cosmic realignment does pull territory with it; each gate-town pulled over adds to the space on the shore of the [[River Styx]]. Accordingly, as you travel from Darkspine to the Styx, you will pass through the ruins of four other previous gate-towns, each older and more destroyed than the last.<ref name="fod26">{{b|Planescape|Fires of Dis|pdf=17273|page=26}}</ref>
In [[125 YFHR]], [[Trias]] the Betrayer, a corrupted [[deva]], enacted a campaign of fear and violence in the gate-town of [[Curst]], causing it to slide into [[Carceri]]. After performing a number of good deeds and defeating Trias, [[The Nameless One]] and his cohorts managed to reverse the realignment, returning Curst to the Outlands.<ref name="pst">{{b|Planescape|Planescape: Torment}}</ref>
In [[126 YFHR]], the Arch-Lector of [[Plague-Mort]], backed by the tanar'ri, attempted to push the gate-town into the [[Abyss]], but the attempt was thwarted.<ref name="wow88105">{{b|Planescape|Well of Worlds|pdf=17269|nip=1|page=88-105}}</ref>
In [[127 YFHR]], the gate-town of [[Fortitude]] was preparing for an event they called the [[Harmonious Ascension]], a purposeful cosmic realignment to bring them to [[Arcadia]]. The pit-fiend [[Zaggutch]], operating on orders from [[Dispater]] himself, enacted a plan to hijack the ceremony mid-realignment by committing evil acts in order to, instead, bring Fortitude to Baator, but the plan failed.<ref name="fod5664">{{b|Planescape|Fires of Dis|pdf=17273|page=56-64}}</ref>
[[Faunel]] has recently crossed over into the [[Beastlands]], leaving settlers to build a new Faunel in its place.<ref name="paitmsato72">{{b|Planescape|Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse|page=72, Sigil and the Outlands}}</ref>
== Effects ==
Several effects of the process of cosmic have been noted, but it's not certain if they're universal or specific to certain locations.
* During the process of realignment, the gate grows in size until it engulfs the city. Fortitude's gate of green flame grew in height until the sky surrounding the city walls was all green flame. * Darkspine was notably a different city from Ribcage, although it's possible that it had previously been called Ribcage and was only renamed after realignment occurred.<ref name="fod25">{{b|Planescape|Fires of Dis|pdf=17273|page=25}}</ref> In other cases (Fortitude, Faunel), the replacement city has the same name as the old. * From the perspective of those in town, the gate may appear to travel to the other plane with them, but they're seeing the "other side" of the gate. Traveling through a gate-town's gate takes you to the previous incarnation of that town on the other plane (e.g. Darkspine), although the state of that location may vary. Thus each Outer Plane has their own corresponding gate-town (or ruins thereof) leading back to the Outlands.<ref name="pcsdmg23">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|page=23, A DM's Guide to the Planes}}</ref> * In some cases, cosmic realignment leaves almost nothing behind, except the gate (Curst, Faunel). However, when Fortitude crosses over, another copy of the city appears, containing similar buildings but different residents.<ref name="fod64">{{b|Planescape|Fires of Dis|pdf=17273|page=64}}</ref>

[[Moon dog]]s | languages = | basicrefs = {{Cite book/Book of Exalted Deeds|150}}{{Cite card/Blood Wars}}{{Cite book/Monstrous Compendium Planescape Appendix II|28}}{{Cite book/Warriors of Heaven|58}}{{Cite dungeon/149/Enemies of My Enemy|57-67}} | type-GW = [[Demiplane]] | shape-size-GW = | gravity-GW = | time-GW = | morphic-GW = | element-energy-GW = | alignment-GW = | magical-GW = | layers-GW = | layer-number-GW = | location-GW = [[Arborea]] | refs-GW = | type-WA = | shape-size-WA = | gravity-WA = | mutability-WA = | element-energy-WA = | alignment-WA = | magical-WA = | layers-WA = | layer-number-WA = | location-WA = | refs-WA = | type-WT = [[Demiplane]] | shape-size-WT = | gravity-WT = | time-WT = Timeless | morphic-WT = | element-energy-WT = | alignment-WT = | magical-WT = | faith-WT = | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = the [[Gates of the Moon]] | refs-WT = {{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|189}} | inhabitants = yes | deities = | locations = yes | organizations = | settlements = | usethe = yes | useon = }} The '''Court of Stars''', sometimes called the '''Court Under the Stars''', was a [[demiplane]] ruled by [[Morwel]], queen of the [[celestial eladrin|eladrin]]. It was the seat of power of the eladrin, but more than that, it represented the essence of the eladrin people. ==Description== The demiplane appeared as a magical, untamed forest in autumn, eternally under a starry sky. (These stars were in fact living entities.) Some of the trees were as thick as houses, and some of the animals, such as [[squirrel]]s, were much larger than elsewhere. [[Fey]] creatures roamed the woods, and at the heart of the realm were the soaring spires of Morwel's crystal palace. Snow could be found at higher altitudes, but the air never felt too cold to tolerate. Time did not pass in the Court of Stars, and as such the inhabitants did not age or need sustenance, although eternal parties were held at the palace and food and drink were freely available for enjoyment. ==Cosmography== The Court of Stars drifted among the three layers of [[Arborea]], only ever appearing at night. It could only be accessed with the express permission of the queen, who was the only one able to open portals to and from the Court. Not even [[Deity|deities]] had access to this demiplane if she did not wish it. Portals to her realm could be found anywhere she wished, such as from [[Corellon Larethian]]'s halls, below the ocean of [[Aquallor]], or in [[Mithardir]]'s sandy wilderness. It was also linked to the [[Gates of the Moon]], [[Selûne]]'s [[divine realm]]. A massive serpentine [[sisiutl]] named [[Triusis]], a servant of the [[archomental]] [[Ben-hadar]] guarded a portal from the [[Plane of Water]] to the Court of Stars.{{Cite dragon/353/Princes of Elemental Good|45}} Another hidden portal to the demiplane was found in [[Niflheim]], where one of the tributaries of the [[River Styx]] came near one of the roots of [[Yggdrasil]]. The portal was opened by touching a sprig of [[mistletoe]] to a scar on a lightning-struck oak tree. ==Notable Locations== Queen Morwel's spired palace was itself transient, continuously phasing in and out of the [[Border Ethereal]]. It could be found at the top of a mountain-sized hill, covered in snow and taller than the clouds. Its massive walls were of glowing crystal. Inside, the palace was lit by countless glittering lights, some of which were magical lanterns, but others were eladrin visitors coming and going in their glowing spherical forms, looking something like sparkling soap bubbles. The central dome of the palace was lit the brightest. It was filled with hundreds of eladrin, standing to floating in globe forms from many tiers around the chamber. At the center sat three golden thrones, where Morwel and her consorts held court. The fabled [[Fountain of Beauty]], also known as [[Evergold]], was also at times reached from the Court of Stars, from a courtyard not far from the spired, crystal palace, but the sacred site shifted from place to place in the multiverse.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|146-147}} ==Defense== The borders of the Court of Stars were defended by forces of [[shiere]]s.{{Cite book/Warriors of Heaven|68}} These were overseen by [[Faerinaal]], the Queen's consort.{{Cite book/Book of Exalted Deeds|153}} ==Inhabitants== Ruling with Morwel in the Court were her consorts, most recently Faerinaal and [[Gwynharwyf]], but Morwel had taken many consorts throughout the centuries. The Court of Stars saw a constant flow of visitors and admirers seeking and audience with the Queen. The realm was also home to many eladrin and fey creatures. [[Moon dog]]s lived here and served as hounds for the eladrin's hunting excursions. ==Rumors & Legends== Morwel never left the Court, and it was rumored that, if she did, the whole realm would collapse. Some believed that the only way to reach the pool of Evergold was through the Court of Stars and only with Queen Morwel's permission. ==Appendix== ===See Also=== * [[Seelie Court]] ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Court of Stars}} {{Arborea}} [[Category:Demiplanes]] [[Category:Planes of existence]] [[Category:Locations in Arborea]] [[Category:Locations in the Gates of the Moon]]
